name: Command Palette
description: A command palette: a search box in a modal dialog, opened with Cmd or Ctrl+K, after the APG combobox with automatic selection. Focus stays in the input, the first result is highlighted so Enter runs it, only the latest search's answer counts, Escape always closes it, and destructive commands ask first.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The palette is a modal: a native <dialog> in the top layer.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a command palette: a search box for destinations and actions in a modal dialog, opened with Cmd or Ctrl+K. It follows the APG combobox with automatic selection: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant marks the highlighted command, and the first result is highlighted so Enter runs it. Only the latest search's answer counts, one status region says the results once typing pauses, Escape always closes it, and destructive commands ask first. Build on the project's command menu or combobox component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Cmd+K on macOS and Ctrl+K elsewhere, without taking over browser shortcuts such as Cmd or Ctrl+P
A native modal <dialog> with a visible Close button; Escape closes it and focus returns to where it was
A combobox input with type="text" controlling a listbox; focus stays in the input, and the first result is highlighted
The arrows wrap through the results in the order on screen; Space types; input methods keep their keys
A highlight with 3:1 contrast that follows the pointer only when it moves
Only the latest search's answer counts, the previous results can't run while a search is out, and one status region says the results once typing pauses
Destructive commands ask first, with focus on Cancel; disabled commands are reachable but don't run
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a command menu or a combobox, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Build the dialog, the search box, and the results (componentSpec.anatomy, frameworkPatterns.searchKeys).
3. Add the shortcut and the optional trigger (implementationDetails.opening).
4. Connect the app's search (frameworkPatterns.latestSearch) and its commands (implementationDetails.running).
5. Add what the task needs: recent commands, groups, scopes, a confirmation step.
6. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, an input method editor, and a phone, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people reach any destination or action from one search box, quickly from the keyboard, without running anything by accident.

anatomy.hierarchy: Optional trigger → dialog (modal, named by its label) → label | input (combobox) | Close | results (listbox: groups and options) | status region; a confirmation step replaces the results for destructive commands

slotNotes.trigger: Cmd+K on macOS and Ctrl+K elsewhere open it. A visible trigger in the header ("Search" or "Commands") shows the shortcut for the person's system, ⌘K or Ctrl K, and has aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K".
slotNotes.dialog: The palette is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), as in the Modal Dialog guide: focus goes into the search box, and the rest of the page is inert.
slotNotes.input: The search box follows the APG combobox with list autocomplete and automatic selection. The input has role="combobox", aria-autocomplete="list", aria-expanded="true" (the list always shows), and aria-controls pointing to the list, and it's labelled "Search commands", visibly or visually hidden. autocomplete="off" and spellcheck="false" keep the browser's suggestions out of the way.
slotNotes.results: The results are a role="listbox" of role="option" rows with unique ids. Groups are role="group" elements, labelled by their headings.
slotNotes.highlight: The highlight is the focus indicator, since focus stays in the input: give it 3:1 contrast against what's around it, with an outline or a solid background. A faint tint such as bg-neutral-100 on white is 1.1:1. Style it from aria-selected or a class, not :focus; options never get focus.
slotNotes.disabledOption: A command that's shown but can't run right now stays reachable with the arrows, has aria-disabled="true", and Enter doesn't run it (APG). Commands the person can never run are left out. Hiding them is only for convenience: the server checks permission when a command runs.
slotNotes.status: While a search is out, the previous results stay in view but can't run: nothing is highlighted, the list has aria-busy="true" (which the project's styles can dim), Enter and clicks do nothing, and the previous announcement is cancelled. Otherwise, with results from a server, Enter in that moment runs a command from the previous query.
slotNotes.confirmation: A destructive command asks first, in a step of the same dialog: the message, then Cancel and a button named for the action ("Delete 3 projects"). Focus goes to Cancel, which is described by the message, and Escape goes back to the results instead of closing the palette.

highlighted.description: The index of the highlighted option in the order on screen, or -1; mirrored in aria-activedescendant. The first result whenever the list changes.

running.description: Whether a command is running; a second Enter does nothing meanwhile.

recent.description: Optional: the ids of recently run commands, shown when the box is empty.
recent.persistence: Storage under the app's own prefix, ids only

interactions.when: Cmd+K on macOS, Ctrl+K elsewhere, unless an editor owns it

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Space types. Until the latest answer arrives, the previous results can't run; only the latest answer fills the list.
Wraps at the ends; disabled commands are reachable. Left to an input method while it composes.
A disabled command doesn't run; a destructive one opens the confirmation step.
The native dialog closes, with text in the box too, and returns focus to the element that had it before. In the confirmation step, Escape goes back to the results instead.
mousedown is cancelled, so focus stays in the input.
Scrolling under a still pointer doesn't move the highlight.

responsiveBehavior.phones: Below 768 px: the dialog fills the screen (100dvh), the search box stays at the top, and only the results scroll.
responsiveBehavior.larger: A centered panel up to 720 px wide, about 12% of the window's height from the top.

variants.global: One palette for the whole app.
variants.scoped: A palette for the current project or workspace, which says so in its label.

commands.shape: { id, label, keywords?, group?, icon?, shortcut?, disabled?, requiresConfirmation?, run() }[]
commands.notes: shortcut is a hint shown next to the label; disabled commands stay reachable; requiresConfirmation opens the confirmation step.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the palette appears without movement.

requirements.1.3.1: The input is a combobox controlling a listbox, groups are labelled, and the dialog is named.
requirements.1.4.3: Labels, hints, and group labels meet 4.5:1 in both themes.
requirements.1.4.11: The highlighted command and focus indicators meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Opening, searching, choosing, and closing all work from the keyboard.
requirements.2.1.2: Escape and Close always leave the palette.
requirements.2.4.3: Focus returns to the element that had it before the palette opened.
requirements.2.4.7: The highlighted command is the visible focus indicator while focus stays in the input.
requirements.3.2.2: Typing never runs a command; only Enter or a click does.
requirements.4.1.2: The combobox exposes its active option; options expose aria-selected and aria-disabled.
requirements.4.1.3: The number of results and failures are announced through one status region.

keyboardNavigation.arrows: Down and Up Arrow move the highlight and wrap at the ends, through the options in the order on screen: build the order from the rendered list, not from the ranked array, since grouping reorders the ranks. Space types, and while an input method composes text, its keys are its own (isComposing, and keyCode 229 in Safari).
keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes the palette, or leaves the confirmation step.
keyboardNavigation.tab: Moves between the search box, Close, and the confirmation step's buttons; the rest of the page is inert.

input.aria-activedescendant: The highlighted option's id, while one is highlighted

option.aria-disabled: true, for a command that can't run right now
option.aria-setsize and aria-posinset: Only when the list renders part of its options

screenReader.highlight: Each highlighted command is read through aria-activedescendant as the list changes or the arrows move.
screenReader.results: The status region says the number of results once typing pauses.

focusManagement.open: The palette is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), as in the Modal Dialog guide: focus goes into the search box, and the rest of the page is inert.
focusManagement.close: Focus returns to the element that had focus before it opened, which the native dialog does by itself (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The shortcut usually opens it, so that isn't the trigger. After a command navigates, focus goes where the new page puts it.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. runCommand() and findCommands() stand for the app's commands and its search; the two scripts share the input, the list, and highlight().

searchKeys.description: The search box, after the APG combobox with automatic selection: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant and aria-selected mark the highlighted command, the arrows wrap, Enter runs, a disabled command doesn't run, input methods keep their keys, a click keeps focus in the input, and the highlight follows the pointer only when it really moves, even in WebKit, which fires pointermove when the list scrolls under a still mouse. type="text", so Escape always closes the dialog.

latestSearch.description: Only the latest search's answer fills the list. While a search is out, the previous results can't run: nothing is highlighted, the list is busy, and the previous announcement is cancelled. When the answer arrives, the first result is highlighted, and the status region says the number of results, "No matching commands", or a failure once typing pauses.

implementationDetails.opening: Cmd+K on macOS and Ctrl+K elsewhere open it. A visible trigger in the header ("Search" or "Commands") shows the shortcut for the person's system, ⌘K or Ctrl K, and has aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K". Don't take over Cmd or Ctrl+P, which is the browser's Print, or other browser shortcuts. When focus is in a rich text editor that uses the same shortcut, the editor keeps it. The palette is a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), as in the Modal Dialog guide: focus goes into the search box, and the rest of the page is inert. Escape closes it, with text in the box too. The input is type="text": in a type="search" field inside a modal dialog, Chromium and Firefox clear the text on the first Escape and keep the palette open, while WebKit closes it at once (checked). Focus returns to the element that had focus before it opened, which the native dialog does by itself (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The shortcut usually opens it, so that isn't the trigger. After a command navigates, focus goes where the new page puts it. A visible Close button is always there, since touch screens and many tablets have no Escape key; a button in a <form method="dialog"> closes the dialog without a script.
implementationDetails.searching: Matching is up to the app: fuzzy matching, keywords and aliases, and ranking by prefix, recent use, and the current context. Matched characters show in bold, not only in color. With an empty box, show recent and suggested commands. Recent commands are kept under the app's own storage prefix, as ids, never with their data. Only the latest search's answer fills the list: number the requests and drop older answers, or abort the previous request. While a search is out, the previous results stay in view but can't run: nothing is highlighted, the list has aria-busy="true" (which the project's styles can dim), Enter and clicks do nothing, and the previous announcement is cancelled. Otherwise, with results from a server, Enter in that moment runs a command from the previous query. One status region, present from the start, says the number of results once typing pauses ("3 commands"), "No matching commands", and failures. It doesn't speak on every key. A long list can render only part of itself; then the highlighted option stays rendered, and every option has aria-setsize and aria-posinset.
implementationDetails.running: A navigation command goes to its page and closes the palette. An action runs; when it succeeds, the palette closes and the outcome goes to the app's status region or a toast. When it fails, the palette stays open with the error in text. A command that opens a dialog closes the palette first, so no dialog opens on top of it. A destructive command asks first, in a step of the same dialog: the message, then Cancel and a button named for the action ("Delete 3 projects"). Focus goes to Cancel, which is described by the message, and Escape goes back to the results instead of closing the palette. While a command runs, a second Enter does nothing.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The palette is a modal: a native <dialog> in the top layer, above sticky bars, dropdowns, and toasts.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. The panel is up to 640 to 720 px wide and about 12% of the window's height from the top; on phones it fills the screen (100dvh), with the search box at the top and only the results scrolling. Rows are 44 px tall, and the input's text is 16 px, so iOS doesn't zoom into it. Text meets 4.5:1 in both themes, shortcut hints and group labels included: text-neutral-500 is only 3.8:1 on a dark panel. Check the project's own colors. Motion is optional: the panel fades in over 150 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, it appears without movement.

edgeCases.noCommands: Say so, and offer a way on, such as the settings or the help page.
edgeCases.manyCommands: Search an index, rank once per query, and render only part of the list.
edgeCases.scopes: A palette for the current project or workspace says so in its label, and lists that context's commands first.

must: Build on the project's command menu or combobox component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Keep focus in the input, with aria-activedescendant for the highlight
Highlight the first result whenever the list changes
Let only the latest search's answer fill the list, and let nothing run from the previous results while a search is out
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a command menu or fuzzy search library, without asking
Use type="search" for the input, or make Escape clear the text instead of closing
Take over Cmd or Ctrl+P, or other browser shortcuts
Move focus into the results, or style the highlight with :focus
Run a disabled command, or a destructive one without asking
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

It's a modal dialog: focus goes into the search box, the rest of the page is inert, and a visible Close button is always there
Escape closes it, even with text in the box, and focus returns to the element that had focus before it opened
The search box is a combobox controlling a listbox; focus stays in it, and aria-activedescendant marks the highlighted command
The first result is highlighted whenever the list changes, so Enter runs it, and the arrows wrap through the results in the order on screen
Space types, and keys that belong to an input method are left to it
The highlighted command has at least 3:1 contrast against what's around it, and follows the pointer only when the pointer moves
A disabled command is reachable with the arrows, and Enter doesn't run it
Only the latest search's answer fills the list, and a failed search says so
While a search is out, the previous results can't run, by Enter or by a click, and nothing is highlighted
One status region says the number of results once typing pauses, and "No matching commands"
A destructive command asks first, with focus on Cancel, and Escape goes back to the results
A command that opens a dialog closes the palette first, and the server checks permission when a command runs
On phones it fills the screen, with 44 px rows and 16 px text
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
